definition: A federal immigration program that allows U.S. agricultural employers to temporarily hire foreign nationals to perform seasonal farm work when not enough domestic workers are available. Employers must follow strict rules protecting both guest workers and American workers in similar jobs, covering wages, housing, and working conditions.
examples: Sun Valley Orchards used the H-2A program to hire temporary agricultural workers and was then accused by the DOL of violating the wage and working conditions requirements that come with participating in the program.
